title: The Wild Crown
premise: Jude Fairweather, a mercenary whose god fell silent three years ago, survives in the city of Vell as a charm-seller in a land where magic is outlawed. When the crown's witch-hunt sweeps him up, he discovers his silence was no accident: he carries the last living spark of the old gods, and the queen intends to burn it out to secure her dynasty's claim. Hunted by an inquisitor who was once his sworn brother, Jude must choose between surrendering the spark to end the persecution of gifted folk or letting it wake and risk reigniting the ancient war between crown and covenant. In the end, Jude gives the spark not to the gods nor the queen, but to the people themselves — breaking the cycle of inheritance and forcing both sides to build something new from the ashes.
about_author: J. M. Thornbury is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval charters before turning to fiction full-time. They write character-driven fantasy about faith, bureaucracy, and the people history forgets.

chapters.title: Small Charms
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. In the market city of Vell, Jude sells luck-knots and fever-charms while hiding the faint pulse of divine power beneath his skin. A routine sale goes wrong when a child's charm actually works in public. Emotional beat: weary caution cracking into fear as Jude realizes he can no longer hide in plain sight.

chapters.title: The Queen's Edict
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Criers announce the Crown Hunt: all gifted persons must register or be burned. Jude watches neighbors denounce each other and weighs flight against the sick sister he supports. Emotional beat: dread hardening into resolve as he begins planning his escape from Vell.

chapters.title: What the God Left Behind
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, with a flashback to the night his god went silent. He examines the spark inside himself for the first time in years and hears, faintly, a word: carry. Emotional beat: grief for his silent god mingling with the terrifying suspicion that he is not abandoned but entrusted.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor
chapters.summary: Sera Vane's POV. The crown's chief inquisitor arrives in Vell — Aldric Renn, once Jude's shield-brother before the god's silence split their order. Sera witnesses Renn's cold efficiency and his private doubt. Emotional beat: unease as she senses the hunt is about more than justice.

chapters.title: Denounced
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A desperate neighbor sells Jude's name to the hunt. Soldiers raid his tenement; he escapes through the rooftops but is forced to leave everything, including medicine for his sister. Emotional beat: guilt and rage at how cheaply loyalty is bought when fear rules.

chapters.title: Road of Ash
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Fleeing north, Jude falls in with a caravan of hidden gifted folk led by Mother Cassia, a former priestess. He conceals the true nature of his spark even as the caravan shelters him. Emotional beat: tentative belonging shadowed by the weight of his secret.

chapters.title: The Covenant's Grave
chapters.summary: Cassia's POV. The caravan reaches a ruined temple of the old order. Cassia recognizes what Jude carries and confronts him privately: the spark is the last fragment of the godhood itself. Emotional beat: awe curdling into terror at what the crown would do — and what waking it might cost.

chapters.title: Brother Against Brother
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. Renn tracks the caravan and recalls his last conversation with Jude before the silence — the argument that broke them. He captures two stragglers and learns Jude travels with them. Emotional beat: longing for the brotherhood they lost warring with his oath to the crown.

chapters.title: Fire in the Wheatfield
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Renn's soldiers ambush the caravan at dawn. Jude reveals his power publicly to save the children, burning a wheatfield and marking himself forever. Emotional beat: exhilaration of unhidden strength followed immediately by horror at the target it paints on everyone near him.

chapters.title: The Queen's Bargain
chapters.summary: Queen Isolde's POV. In the capital, the queen learns a carrier has been found. She offers amnesty to all registered gifted if the carrier is delivered — a trap designed to turn the persecuted against Jude. Emotional beat: cold pragmatism masking her own fear that her throne rests on a lie.

chapters.title: Split Roads
chapters.summary: Cassia's POV. The caravan debates surrendering Jude for amnesty. Cassia argues truth over safety; others vote to send word to the crown. Jude leaves voluntarily rather than force the choice. Emotional beat: bitter disillusionment — loyalty proves conditional when survival is priced in.

chapters.title: The Silent Order
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude seeks the remnants of his mercenary order in the mountains, hoping their old oaths still bind. He finds only three survivors, including one who knows why the gods went silent: they poured themselves into carriers to survive the first war. Emotional beat: revelation reframing his abandonment as sacrifice.

chapters.title: What Renn Remembers
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. Renn interrogates the captured stragglers and finds Cassia's testimony about the spark planted doubt. He requests the queen's private archives and discovers records of the first war — and the crown's original crime. Emotional beat: faith fracturing as duty and truth pull apart.

chapters.title: The Archive Beneath
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera helps Renn break into the sealed archive and reads the true history: the royal line seized power by slaughtering the gods' vessels centuries ago. She must decide whether to report Renn's findings. Emotional beat: a bureaucrat's awakening — the machinery she served runs on buried blood.

chapters.title: Hunted Together
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The order's survivors are betrayed; Renn corners Jude but cannot strike, and instead demands answers. Jude shows him the memory of the god's final word. Emotional beat: enemies standing weapon-to-weapon, the old bond flickering back to life in the space between blows.

chapters.title: The Turning of Aldric Renn
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. Renn burns his warrant and defects, bringing evidence of the crown's crime. But Sera, torn, has already reported the archive breach. Emotional beat: costly redemption — choosing truth means becoming hunted alongside the man he swore to take.

chapters.title: City of Chains
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. The trio infiltrates Vell, now under martial law, to reach the sister Jude abandoned and the network Cassia built. Emotional beat: homecoming turned siege — every street holds either a friend pretending not to know them or a neighbor ready to sell them.

chapters.title: The Queen's Altar
chapters.summary: Queen Isolde's POV. The queen prepares a rite to burn the spark out of Jude upon capture, believing only its destruction will make her claim permanent. Her young heir asks an innocent question about the gods that she cannot answer honestly. Emotional beat: a ruler confronting the hollowness of an inheritance built on erasure.

chapters.title: The Burning Square
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Captured in Vell, Jude is sentenced to public immolation. As the pyre is lit, the crowd of registered gifted — spared by amnesty but branded — begins to sing the old hymns. The spark answers. Emotional beat: despair transfigured into collective defiance as the silenced find their voice through him.

chapters.title: Crown of Embers
chapters.summary: Jude and Aldric's alternating POV. The spark fully wakes; the queen's rite backfires, and the ancient war threatens to reignite as the god's power surges toward vengeance. Jude wrestles it down, refusing to become the weapon history expects. Emotional beat: climax — the hardest victory is restraint, choosing mercy over righteous fire.

chapters.title: The Giving
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Before the assembled crown, covenant remnants, and common folk, Jude does the unthinkable: he releases the spark into the crowd, dividing it among thousands so no king, priest, or carrier can ever own it again. The god speaks one last time — not through him, but through everyone. Emotional beat: grief and liberation entwined as Jude surrenders the thing that defined him.

chapters.title: After the Silence
chapters.summary: Sera's POV, closing with Jude's. A year later: the queen abdicates to her heir under a new charter, magic is licensed rather than outlawed, and Renn plants a garden on the old pyre ground. Jude, ordinary at last, sells honest charms in Vell — and sometimes, faintly, the whole market hums. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — inheritance transformed from burden into shared breath.
